title: Drone Flythrough
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a drone-style camera flythrough along a CatmullRomCurve3, with a simplified outdoor scene and POIs.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
</script>

[Scene]
(1) A large ground plane, one road (a dark, elongated plane), 10 trees (Cylinder trunks + Cone canopies), and 5 buildings (Boxes of different heights).

[Path]
(2) Use CatmullRomCurve3 with at least 10 control points; the curve may be closed or open. Set the camera position along the curve using getPoint(t), with t advanced based on time and speed.

[Controls]
(3) id="playBtn": toggle between play and pause (either change the button text or use aria-pressed).
(4) id="speedSlider": a range of approximately 0.2–3.0 that controls the speed multiplier for progression along the path.
(5) id="pathProgress": a range of 0–1 (or 0–100 normalized to 0–1 in the state), displays the current path parameter and can be dragged to jump to a different path parameter; keep it synchronized with the current t.
(6) id="manualOverrideToggle": a checkbox that, when checked, enables OrbitControls (or similar) for manual camera control and pauses automatic movement along the path; when unchecked, resumes path following.

[POIs]
(7) 5 spheres with text labels (using Sprites or HTML overlays). Clicking one displays information; the div with id="poiInfo" displays the current POI name and description.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  pathProgress: number,
  speed: number,
  isPaused: boolean,
  currentPOI: string | null,
  cameraPos: { x: number, y: number, z: number },
  poiCount: number
}

Output a single HTML file that can be run by opening it directly in a browser.
